sentences.text: The name Ignotosaurus means 'unknown lizard' because only a single right ilium fossil is known.
This known fossil is an ilium approximately 70 mm long, making the total size of the animal difficult to determine accurately.
The specific name 'fragilis' refers to the ilium's blade, which has a central portion only 1 mm thick.
The ilium has a saddle-shaped lateral profile and is longer than it is deep.
A supraacetabular crest runs laterally along the bone and assists in forming the socket where the femur attaches.
The preacetabular process is angled at 90 degrees to the iliac blade and points anterolaterally, serving as a diagnostic feature of the species.
The genus Ignotosaurus was described by Martínez and colleagues in 2013.
The type species of the genus is Ignotosaurus fragilis.
Ignotosaurus was likely a herbivore that competed for food with rhynchosaurs, cynodonts, and early dinosaurs in river basin habitats.
Ignotosaurus is thought to be closely related to Silesaurus, Sacisaurus, and Eucoelophysis, though this is uncertain due to limited fossil evidence.
Ignotosaurus lived between 237 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
Ignotosaurus lived during the Late Triassic (Carnian) in northwestern Argentina alongside early dinosaurs like Herrerasaurus.
